content: The day which we fear as our last is but the birthday of eternity.
author: Seneca
story:
Having survived eight years of political exile on the barren island of Corsica and the volatile, lethal court of Emperor Nero, Seneca understood the fragility of fortune and the necessity of philosophical armor. Writing to his companion Lucilius, he urged immediate, courageous living over anxious anticipation of future disasters.

This insight points directly back to the quiet center of being. Seneca observed that while the mind perpetually scatters itself into past regrets and future anxieties, peace is only ever discovered by anchoring attention in the immediate truth of this moment.
reflectionPrompt: What quiet yearning in your heart is asking for your attention and honest devotion?
